instruction: Please install the unpacked Chrome extension from the helloExtension folder on the Desktop into the browser.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: Task requires installing an unpacked Chrome extension from Desktop. Evaluator checks if the extension path '/home/user/Desktop/helloExtension' appears in the list of unpacked extension paths. Uses existing getter 'get_find_unpacked_extension_path' which reads Chrome Preferences and extracts all extension paths. Postconfig sleep added to ensure Chrome has sufficient time to write extension installation to Preferences file.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: get_find_unpacked_extension_path (chrome.py:1401-1436) reads Chrome Preferences file and extracts all extension paths from extensions.settings[id].path, returning a list of all installed extension paths
Metric logic is correct: is_in_list (general.py:76-81) checks if expected value is in result list using 'expect in result', which is the correct list membership check
Data flow is correct: getter extracts list of extension paths -> metric checks if expected path '/home/user/Desktop/helloExtension' is in that list
Expected value is semantically correct: '/home/user/Desktop/helloExtension' matches the setup config which unzips helloExtension.zip to /home/user/Desktop/
Complete coverage: evaluator verifies the single requirement - that the unpacked extension from the specified folder is installed in Chrome

State accessibility is correct: getter reads from Chrome Preferences file (persistent state), not from UI, so no UI-dependent postconfig is needed. The 2-second sleep in postconfig is sufficient for Chrome to write to Preferences
Logic will work correctly at runtime: straightforward file read from JSON Preferences file and list membership check
